description: What a number measures. A unit does not say it: a megajoule can be net calorific value, gross calorific value, or a heat of combustion whose basis nobody stated, and uranium's megajoules are not a heat of combustion at all. One row per quantity a source list can state about one of its own flows (`*-property-statements.json`), keyed by `slug`. `quantity_kind_iri` is the kind a statement's `unit` must belong to, in the spelling `units.json` uses; `ilcd_flow_property_uuid` is the ILCD flow property the quantity is the same thing as, where ILCD has one -- EF 3.1 ships these under `flow-properties.json`; `qudt_match` is the published QUDT quantity kind and how this row relates to it, looked up in the QUDT vocabulary on 2026-10-24 and never inferred. The canonical labels are ILCD's; the other spellings are aliases the vendor parsers match on.

quantities.label: Mass
quantities.definition: How much of the flow there is by weight. Stated per unit volume of a flow measured in cubic metres it is the flow's density, which is why the density spellings are aliases here: a vendor saying `Specific weight: 650 kg/m3` is saying one cubic metre of this wood is 650 kg.

quantities.label: Volume
quantities.definition: How much of the flow there is by the space it takes up. Stated per kilogram of a flow measured by mass it is the inverse of its density: one kilogram of fresh water is 0.001 cubic metres.

quantities.label: Net calorific value
quantities.definition: The heat released when a unit of the flow is burnt, not counting the latent heat of the water the combustion forms. What EF 3.1 measures its 34 energy flows in, and the lower of a fuel's two heating values. QUDT's `HeatingValue` does not split net from gross, so this is a narrower term of it.

quantities.label: Gross calorific value
quantities.definition: The heat released when a unit of the flow is burnt and the water the combustion forms is condensed, so its latent heat is counted. The higher of a fuel's two heating values; what Stepwise 2006's method converts by.

quantities.label: Calorific value, basis unstated
quantities.definition: A heat of combustion whose source does not say whether it is net or gross: ecoinvent's 18.01 MJ/kg for hard coal, read off its EF 3.1 implementation workbook. Kept apart from the two stated bases so that the gap is visible rather than guessed at; it converts onto either, and the mapping says the basis was unstated.

quantities.label: Fission energy
quantities.definition: The energy a unit of a nuclear fuel yields by fission -- 560,000 MJ per kilogram of natural uranium, which ecoinvent documents as a gross fission energy content. Not a heat of combustion, so it never shares a quantity with a calorific value and never converts onto one. EF 3.1 labels its `Uranium` flow's megajoule a net calorific value; the base list's statements file corrects that flow's reference quantity to this. QUDT has no per-mass fission kind, so this is a narrower term of its `SpecificEnergy`.

quantities.label: Radioactivity
quantities.definition: How many nuclei of the flow decay per second. Stated per kilogram of a flow measured by mass it is the isotope's specific activity, which follows from its half-life: a kilogram of radium-226 is 3.66e10 kilobecquerels.
